steps.body: When the ones run short, break one ten open: it becomes ten ones, and the tens column has one fewer ten.
steps.narration: When the ones run short, break one ten open: it becomes ten ones, and the tens column has one fewer ten.

widget.prompt: Show 43 broken for subtraction: 3 rods and 13 cubes.

commonBuilds.feedback: 4 rods and 13 cubes make 53 — the broken ten must LEAVE the tens place.

widget.missFeedback: That build names a different number — total each unit's worth and match 43 exactly.
widget.successFeedback: 3 rods and 13 cubes still make 43 — the opened ten just wears a different form.

predict.prompt: You break a ten into ten ones. What happens to the total?
predict.reveal: Breaking renames a ten as ten ones; the value moves, it never shrinks.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2b break ten.
invariants: Trading between places changes the FORM of a quantity, never its value — the model and the number must stay equal for g2b break ten.
misconceptions: Treating a trade as adding or removing amount instead of renaming the same total.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the blocks stop matching the written number?

explanationVariants: Open a ten into ten ones.

commonErrors.feedback: The broken ten was never removed from the tens place — after opening it, one fewer ten remains.
That flipped the ones to "big minus small" (5 − 4); the ten must be broken instead.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Line the places up — hundreds with hundreds, tens with tens, ones with ones — and work one column at a time.

widget.prompt: While solving with 338, a student trades ten ones for a ten. Why is that allowed?

options.label: Because ten ones and one ten are equal amounts
options.feedback: Correct — the trade is legal exactly because both forms name the same quantity.

options.label: Because the answer gets bigger
options.feedback: A valid trade never changes the total at all — that is the whole point of it.

options.label: Because tens look nicer than ones
options.feedback: Looks are not the reason; equal VALUE is what licenses the swap.

options.label: Because subtraction requires it every time
options.feedback: Many subtractions need no trade; the trade appears only when a place runs short.
